# Accessing and Cloning Your `hw02` Repository

::: {.callout-important}
This will work only if you have submitted your GitHub username and email (see Lecture 1). Accept the email invitation to join our GitHub organization OR simply open the assignment link below, which accepts the invitation for you. Make sure you have completed the setup under [Software Setup](../setup/index.qmd) and confirmed everything works properly.
:::

### Accessing the repo

1. Go to [this link](https://classroom50.org/css-fall26/css/assignments/hw02/accept). The first time, click *Sign in with GitHub* and authorize Classroom 50 (the tool we use to distribute assignments).

2. Click *Accept assignment* to create your private `hw02` repository on GitHub. Your repository will be named `css-hw02-<USERNAME>`. Keep the page open until the setup checklist finishes (a few seconds).

3. Click *Open repository* to access it.

If the page says *"Not a member yet"*, accept the invitation to our GitHub organization (check your email, including spam), then click *Check again*. If it says *"This assignment isn't available to you"*, contact the instructor.


### Cloning the repo into your Workbench

1. Log into *Workbench* and start a new project:  
   *File > New Project > Version Control > Git*

2. In the *Repository URL* field:
   - Paste the URL of your GitHub repository. To find the URL, go to your `hw02` repo on GitHub, click the green Code button, and copy the SSH or HTTPS link (use the method you configured during setup: Workbench users must select SSH).
   - The project name should auto-fill. If not, type the same name manually (it should match the GitHub repo name).

3. Choose where to save the project directory locally. *Tip:* Avoid moving folders after cloning them.  

4. Check the box *"Open in new session"* (recommended for keeping projects organized).

5. Click *Create Project*. This will:
   - Create a new folder on your machine  
   - Initialize a Git repository linked to GitHub  
   - Open an RStudio Project in a new session

You’ll use this same process to access and set up each homework assignment throughout the course.

# HW2 Description

### The mass shooting dataset

The United States experiences far more mass shooting events than any other developed country in the world. Policymakers, politicians, the media, activists, and the general public acknowledge the widespread prevalence of these events. However, effective policies to prevent such incidents should be grounded in empirical data.

In July 2012, in the aftermath of a mass shooting in a movie theater in Aurora, Colorado,
[Mother Jones](https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2012/07/mass-shootings-map/) published a report on mass shootings in the United States since 1982. Importantly, they provided the underlying data set as [an open-source database](https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2012/12/mass-shootings-mother-jones-full-data/) for anyone interested in studying and understanding the topic.

This dataset is already installed on Workbench.

### Answer the questions

Your repository includes specific and open-ended questions. Answer all of them.

::: {.callout-note}

- The questions, especially the open-ended ones, are designed to help you think like a programmer and data analyst. They won’t walk you through every step but encourage you to apply what you’ve learned and work independently. Translating what a question asks into code by breaking it down in smaller pieces is one important learning goal of this exercise

- This homework is designed to be completed over multiple sessions. Start early, and remember to save, commit, and push your work regularly.

- Do not use AI tools to generate R code from scratch or think for you. You may use it to debug (after trying on your own) or look up how functions work, but check course materials first. Only submit code you fully understand. Reach out if you have questions, we are here to help!

# Formatting Guide for All Homework

This guide applies to all your homework assignments and the final project. **Please, use it to format your graphs and tables** in this and future assignments.

### Formatting graphs

Your final graphs should be appropriate for sharing with outsiders. That means your graphs should have:

* [A title](http://r4ds.had.co.nz/graphics-for-communication.html#label)
* Labels on the axes (type `?labs` in your Console for details)
* Consider adopting your own color scales, [taking control of your legends (if any)](http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/Legends_(ggplot2)/), playing around with [themes](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/index.html#section-themes), and generally customizing your graphs to improve their visual appeal and clarity.


### Formatting tables

When presenting tabular data, consider using the `kable()` function from the `knitr` package to format the table for the final document. Here is how you use this function.

The code below displays a basic table summarizing where gun deaths occurred:
```{r packages, message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(rcis)
```

```{r table-bad, echo = TRUE}
# calculate total gun deaths by location
count(mass_shootings, location_type)
```

This is the same code but we added `kable()` to format the table, add a caption, and label the columns. Observe what it does:
```{r table-good, format = "asis", echo = TRUE}
count(mass_shootings, location_type) %>%
  kable(
    caption = "Mass shootings in the United States by location",
    col.names = c("Location", "Number of incidents")
  )
```

Run `?kable` in your Console for additional options

# How to Submit this Assignment

To submit your assignment on Canvas, follow these steps:

1. Before the deadline, push the final version of your work to your GitHub repository. *Tip:* don’t wait until the end to make your first commit; instead stage, commit, and push your work regularly as you go.

   Your GitHub repository should include:
   - `mass-shootings.Rmd`: main file you work on, remember to add your name at the top
   - `mass-shootings.md`: you will generate this file from the `.Rmd` by knitting it, like you did for HW01. The output format is already set to `github_document` keep it that way unless you encounter problems, in which case contact us
   - `mass-shootings_files/`: this folder contains all the graphs that you generated in your `.Rmd`

2. When you're ready to submit:
   - Copy the URL of your GitHub repository. It will look something like: `https://github.com/css-fall26/css-hw02-yourusername`
   - Submit that URL on Canvas under HW02. Do not upload any files to Canvas. We only need the repository link. Your repository remains private, only the instructional staff can access it.
